note: The viewer-interoperability file set for `python -m nctool viewer set` (scripts/viewer-interop/README.md). Every destination case of benchmark.json's `fixtures` set that names a destination (`--range` or `--film-master`), applied to each input below. A chart input reuses acceptance.json's input of that name; a roll input is rendered under the recipe `hanten measure-roll` writes for its roll (the roll's real frames, with its unexposed frame and leader). `expect` is what the rubric checks per encoding: `rendition` is item 2, `fallback` item 3 (gated only where `fallback_gated`), `readers` who opens it, once per display setting (`true` where HDR is on). `hdr` marks an encoding whose item 2 is an HDR rendition, so with HDR off item 3 replaces it.

chart.why: known patches and a neutral ramp; no personal content

ektar-1627.why: three clearly different channel gains (about 4.9 / 4.4 / 3.3), so a reader that uses one channel shows it

gold-1144.why: highlights reach the HDR peak on every channel, so the headroom ceiling is exercised

hdr-linear-tiff.rendition: HDR: highlights brighter than SDR white on an HDR display
hdr-linear-tiff.fallback: not specified: record what the reader shows

hdr-pq-tiff.rendition: HDR: highlights brighter than SDR white on an HDR display
hdr-pq-tiff.fallback: not specified: record what the reader shows

hdr-hlg-tiff.rendition: HDR: highlights brighter than SDR white on an HDR display
hdr-hlg-tiff.fallback: not specified: record what the reader shows

gain-map-jpeg.rendition: HDR on an HDR display (the gain map applied)
gain-map-jpeg.fallback: the SDR base image, matching the SDR TIFF of the same gamut in tone

film-master.rendition: not a display rendition (scene-linear ACEScg): record what the reader shows
film-master.fallback: not specified: record what the reader shows
